title: Hypersimplicity and truth-table completeness
summary: Prove hypersimple sets truth-table incomplete and construct a simple set truth-table equivalent to halting by filling computable intervals.
abstract: A simple enumerable set cannot encode every enumerable problem by a single computable translation. A finite table of membership answers can do more: we construct a simple set from which such a table decides the halting problem. Each computable interval initially contains a guaranteed omission from the earlier Post simple set, and halting determines which intervals are filled. Hypersimple sets obey a stronger restriction on their omitted numbers. We prove that truth-table access to halting would produce computable disjoint intervals each containing an omission, contradicting hypersimplicity. The proof makes the required formula construction and its uniform program indices explicit, distinguishing the limitations of simplicity from those of hypersimplicity.
